entry.content:

  • Pitcher 'no data': Pitchers only have a pNERD score once they've started at least one game and have at least 20 innings pitched. I also show 'no data' when I can't correctly link a starting pitcher with their stats.
  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Minnesota Twins @ Milwaukee Brewers, 11:10a

Summary

Jacob Misiorowski is must-watch, and even a highly imbalanced pitching matchup can't drag this one below elite territory for a Sunday getaway game. The Brewers' rookie phenom brings a video-game stat line into this one — he's leading the league in ERA, FIP, strikeouts, WHIP, and K/BB ratio, and sits at 11-5 with a 1.63 ERA with his sights on potentially crossing the 200-strikeout threshold. His pNERD of 15.96 is essentially off the charts — miles above today's average of 5.36 and even above the historic 95th percentile — built on absurd swinging-strike and xFIP- numbers paired with a fastball touching triple digits. Across the diamond, Wisconsin native Connor Prielipp is having a solid rookie year overall (6.37 pNERD, above average) but has scuffled lately, allowing three runs in five-plus innings against Seattle most recently. Milwaukee's tNERD of 9.85 is near the top of the league, fueled by strong baserunning and one of the best bullpens around, while Minnesota's offense limps in without Byron Buxton, who's on the injured list since late July with a right hip impingement. With a gNERD of 17.43 — comfortably above today's slate and among the best games recently — this is the one to prioritize if you just want to watch someone make big-league hitters look silly.

Atlanta Braves @ New York Yankees, 10:35a

Summary

Good stuff for a decent summary. Now write it.

A rubber match at Yankee Stadium with real playoff-atmosphere stakes and one of the better pitching mismatches you'll find on the schedule. New York has already banked the first two games of this series—Gerrit Cole allowed just two earned runs over seven innings in Saturday's win, and Tanner Mahle held the Braves to two runs in Friday's opener—and now sends out Cam Schlittler, who's quietly been the Yankees' most reliable arm in the second half with a sub-2.30 ERA and 171 strikeouts. His pNERD of 10.47 checks out: mid-90s heat that actually touches 98, a chase-inducing slider, and an xFIP- nearly 30% better than league average all point to a legitimately dominant start. Grant Holmes is fine, not flashy—his pNERD of 3.28 reflects a middling swinging-strike rate and shaky command. The juicier subplot is Atlanta's lineup, with Ronald Acuna Jr. back from a hamstring injury and swinging it well, having gone deep twice and driven in three runs recently. Both tNERD marks sit comfortably above average, with the Yankees' barrel rate and baserunning standing out. At 14.01, this gNERD lands well above the historical median and close to today's top tier—worth carving out time for.

New York Mets @ Pittsburgh Pirates, 10:35a

Summary

Both teams sit under .500, but this rubber match still packs punch thanks to Jared Jones. The Pirates just throttled the Mets 9-0 in the series' penultimate game, and Pittsburgh desperately needed that offensive outburst, which snapped a four-game losing streak, and now try to string wins together for the first time in two weeks. Jones is the headliner here—his 98.4 mph average fastball velocity and elite swinging-strike rate produce a pNERD of 10.00, comfortably above today's slate average, and his July was terrific: 27 innings, 33 strikeouts and six walks across five starts, though his last outing was a clunker against Milwaukee. Manaea, by contrast, is merely solid; he's been one of the Mets' more effective starters over the past month, picking up a win against Cleveland by allowing two runs over six innings with seven strikeouts, aided by an uncharacteristic velocity bump. On the team side, Pittsburgh's 7.03 tNERD edges New York's 5.34, fueled by strong baserunning and a payroll-underdog scrappiness that contrasts with the Mets' star-studded, high-priced roster. Add it up and you get a 13.73 gNERD—solidly above both the historic and today's averages—making this one worth a look, mostly for Jones' arm.

Cleveland Guardians @ Chicago White Sox, 11:10a

Summary

Cleveland at Chicago closes a tense weekend set with real division stakes, and both starters have been quietly steady, making this an above-average watch even without fireworks. The White Sox actually sit atop the AL Central, with Cleveland trying to close the gap; the two teams split the first two games, with Chicago winning 6-3 on Saturday after Cleveland took the opener 8-2 on Friday, so the rubber match carries weight. Cantillo and Martin both grade out in solid-average territory (pNERD 5.41 and 5.04), each backed by respectable xFIP- marks in the mid-90s rather than gaudy strikeout stuff — competent rather than thrilling. The lineups provide the juice: Cleveland's José Ramírez remains a threat with 28 stolen bases and 52 runs, while Chicago counters with Munetaka Murakami's 26 home runs and a productive Vargas/Montgomery combo. Both clubs post tNERD scores near 7.4-7.8, comfortably above the historical average, thanks largely to young, discount payrolls rather than star power. Combined, the 12.82 gNERD lands solidly above the historical median and roughly in line with today's slate average — a division scrap worth a look, if not a must-see.

Cincinnati Reds @ Washington Nationals, 9:15a

Summary

A high-scoring team battle wrapped around two shaky, low-strikeout stuff arms — watch for the offense, not the pitching duel. Washington's 9.41 tNERD is one of the stronger scores of the day, fueled by a team .765 OPS against Cincinnati's .710 OPS, and the Nats arrive having won three of four after dropping a season-worst seven in a row, including Saturday's 8-2 win that snapped Cincinnati ace Chase Burns' 12-game winning streak. Cincinnati's bullpen is the drag on their tNERD, ranking as one of the league's worst run-prevention pens. On the mound, Brad Lord (pNERD 6.00) is stretching out after going on the 15-day injured list with side tightness and making his return in relief before this spot start — he's also historically owned the Reds, going 1-0 with a 2.35 ERA in two games (one start) against the Reds. Brady Singer (pNERD 4.32) has been hittable all year and has been dreadful specifically against Washington, sporting a 9.82 ERA in three starts against the Nationals. The 12.55 gNERD sits comfortably above the historic average — worth a look for the lineups alone.

Detroit Tigers @ San Francisco Giants, 1:05p

Summary

A hot young arm meets a former ace trying to rediscover his form, and the NERD math actually backs up the hype. Troy Melton, Detroit's 25-year-old righty, has been the story of the Tigers' rotation shake-up—he's hasn't lost since June 25 and just turned in back-to-back seven-inning shutout efforts, allowing 6 hits and four walks while striking out nine for a 2.66 FIP and a 0.71 WHIP. That production, plus a mid-90s fastball and a strong xFIP-, gives him a 7.55 pNERD, comfortably above average. Across the mound, Logan Webb is trying to climb out of a rough patch—a bit of a down year by his standards after a rough July with a bloated 6.59 ERA—but he answered with a shutout start against Texas, and his elite ground-ball, low-xFIP profile still earns a solid pNERD of 5.76. Team-wise, both clubs are middling on paper, though Detroit's fading wild-card push adds stakes while San Francisco is playing out the season but has already shown this week it can compete with a team chasing October. At 11.19, the gNERD sits just above the historical average and near today's midpoint—a solid, watchable pitching-forward matchup rather than a must-see event.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Arizona Diamondbacks, 1:10p

Summary

Good history matchup this is: Dodgers vs. Diamondbacks, and it's Wrobleski due for a bounce-back while Rodriguez has owned LA all year, but the numbers say this is a middling watch, not a must-see.

Justin Wrobleski, an All-Star this season, enters after a rocky stretch — he allowed four home runs in each of his last two outings, matching his total from his first 17 games and 106 2/3 innings this season. His pNERD of 6.47 is buoyed by a quick pace and youth, though a middling xFIP- and low swinging-strike rate keep him from elite territory. Eduardo Rodriguez, meanwhile, owns this matchup — the Diamondbacks have won both of Rodríguez's starts against the Dodgers this season, with him going six innings on both June 1 and July 10 with a total of three runs allowed — but his pNERD sits at just 2.60, dragged down by an above-average xFIP- and shaky command. The Dodgers' 8.67 tNERD, powered by strong batting and barrel rates, dwarfs Arizona's 4.40, giving this game a tNERD gap that favors star power (Ohtani, Freeman, Tucker) over balance. At 11.07, the gNERD lands just above the historical median and slightly below today's slate average — watchable, particularly for the Wrobleski redemption arc, but not essential.

Los Angeles Angels @ Miami Marlins, 10:40a

Summary

Not exactly appointment viewing, but the Marlins' scrappy roster gives it a pulse. The Angels (45-72, an ugly 20-39 on the road) roll into Miami for the rubber match of a series that's tied 1-1, and it's the third time these teams square off this season. Grayson Rodriguez, acquired from Baltimore in the offseason in exchange for Taylor Ward after missing the 2025 season recovering from right elbow surgery to remove bone spurs, has struggled mightily in his return, sporting a rough 7.24 ERA and 1.59 WHIP — his 4.15 pNERD reflects mediocre stuff (subpar swinging-strike rate) partly offset by a big velocity mismatch with his results, suggesting some positive regression is possible. Ryan Gusto's ugly 0-3 record hides better process — an xFIP- of 98 and a decent strike rate give him the higher pNERD of the two. The real story is Miami's tNERD of 9.05, nearly the day's ceiling, built on a young, cheap roster with strong baserunning, bullpen, and fielding marks — the Angels' 1.02 tNERD is the anti-Marlins, bottom-of-the-barrel almost everywhere. Overall gNERD of 9.82 sits right around the historical middle — watchable mostly for Miami's vibe, not Anaheim's.

Kansas City, at a meager 2.75 tNERD, is the driftwood here — the Royals offense has been below average this season (95 wRC+, 21st in MLB), even worse in the second half (89 wRC+), and their bullpen (-2.61) is one of the worst pieces in this whole dataset. On the mound, Matthew Boyd (pNERD 5.00) has quietly been one of the better lefties in the league since Boyd will look to continue his strong performance since coming off the IL, pairing a healthy strike rate with average stuff. Randy Dobnak (pNERD 2.13) is the stranger story: a 1.16 ERA that's wildly out of step with a 4.22 FIP, because his walk and strikeout rates are both pretty horrible, but he is a groundball machine — that's run-prevention smoke and mirrors that shows up as a below-average pNERD. Overall gNERD of 9.77 sits a shade under the historic median, and squarely below today's slate average, so slot this one in as a background game unless you enjoy watching a good team feast on a broken bullpen.

Detail

Atlanta Braves @ New York Yankees, 12:05p

Summary

Chris Sale on extra rest against a Yankees offense that can't buy a hit right now—this is as good as pitching matchups get on a Saturday. The gNERD score of 15.32 sits near the top of the historical range and above today's average, and it's easy to see why: Sale, fresh off National League Pitcher of the Month honors in July, carries a 9.47 pNERD thanks to elite xFIP-, sharp swinging-strike numbers, and velocity that at age 37 is somehow still climbing, with his manager crediting extra rest between starts. "(Extra rest) is one of the things that has kept him strong and kept his velocity where it's at," Braves manager Walt Weiss said, "It's crazy to think about, but at 37 years old, he's producing some of the highest velocities of his career. Cole brings a respectable 6.75 pNERD, with mid-90s heat and strong strike-throwing, though his sinker has been a genuine liability and the Yankees' offense has been ice-cold for weeks, setting up a strength-on-weakness clash against Atlanta's power bats. The Braves also arrive having just seen their season-high eight-game winning streak end when Atlanta blew a save, with Austin Riley and Matt Olson both going deep in that loss. Both tNERDs sit comfortably above average, with the Yankees' barrel rate and baserunning giving them a slight edge. This is a marquee pitching duel worth clearing your schedule for.

Cleveland Guardians @ Chicago White Sox, 4:40p

Summary

Cleveland's on a three-game losing streak and just got run out of town by the Mets, while Chicago is nursing bruises from a four-hour, 13-inning heartbreaker against Boston — so this AL Central tilt has a "please just get through this weekend" energy that oddly makes it more watchable, not less. The headline is the rookie lefty duel: Noah Schultz is slated to start for the White Sox against fellow left-hander Parker Messick in a duel of rookies. Messick has been the real deal, backed by strong strikeout and command marks that drive his 7.68 pNERD, and his tidy xFIP- makes him one of the more efficient young arms around. Schultz, still just 22, throws hard at 95-plus but has been homer-prone and wild in the zone, with an xFIP- that lags his shiny recent outing — his negative luck value hints some correction toward better results is plausible. Both rosters skew young and cheap, which the tNERD payroll and age components reward, pushing Chicago's team score toward the top of today's range. At 13.53, this game's gNERD sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages — worth carving out time for.

Minnesota Twins @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

Milwaukee's bullpen is red-hot and Minnesota's defense is a mess, which pretty much tells you everything about why this game leans watchable despite two names casual fans won't recognize. The Brewers own the NL's best record and are riding a three-game home winning streak, with a tNERD of 9.44 fueled by strong baserunning, a deep bullpen, and a young, cost-effective roster. Minnesota, by contrast, is a middling road team with negative marks in fielding and baserunning, dragging their tNERD down to 2.61. On the mound, Shane Drohan gets the spotlight: since debuting this April, he's been the superior arm here, and he has reliably pitched six innings the last month or so, posting a 3.48 ERA and 3.02 FIP with 89 strikeouts this season, and this is his first career appearance against Minnesota. Zebby Matthews, freshly recalled from Triple-A after Joe Ryan's IL stint, brings positive pNERD largely from good luck and velocity rather than dominant peripherals — betting markets and prop analysts favor Drohan's cleaner strikeout profile. At 12.78, the gNERD sits comfortably above the historical median, making this an above-average, if not electric, watch.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

The Brewers are running away with the NL Central and now get to face a Cy Young winner who's quietly been scuffling — this one's got both star power and a legitimate "can Skenes fix himself" storyline. Paul Skenes carries a gaudy 156 strikeouts and 1.11 WHIP into the start, but he's been rocked for a combined 10 runs in 9 1/3 innings in his past two starts, ballooning his ERA to 3.90 — a rare rough patch for a pitcher whose underlying stuff (upper-90s velocity, elite whiff rate) still grades out as one of the best in baseball, evidenced by his 10.98 pNERD. Opposite him, Kyle Harrison makes his first start since landing on the IL with forearm tightness back on July 11, adding some rust-shaking intrigue to an already loaded pitching matchup — his 10.63 pNERD is nearly identical to Skenes'. Milwaukee, at 9.25 tNERD, brings the best record in baseball, plus strong baserunning and a bullpen that grades out as one of the league's better units. Add it up and you get an 18.92 gNERD, comfortably above both the historical 95th percentile (14.76) and today's slate average — this is the game to watch.

Miami Marlins @ Atlanta Braves, 4:15p

Summary

Good under-the-radar arm show tucked into a division race, with Eury Pérez's triple-digit heat pushing the day's top pitcher NERD in this matchup. Atlanta enters on a roll, having taken game one of this series 4-2 behind Ozzie Albies and Austin Riley homers, and now looking to extend their winning streak to a season-high seven games against a Miami club that's road-weary and shorthanded. Pérez brings a 98.2 mph average heater and a strikeout-heavy profile that anchors his 7.62 pNERD, the better of the two starters today, while Grant Holmes carrying six scoreless innings before Austin Riley's two-run shot sealed it in Tuesday's opener shows Atlanta's rotation depth even without Chris Sale and an injured Reynaldo López. Elder counters with a serviceable 4.94 pNERD, buoyed by a quick pace but dinged by middling swing-and-miss stuff; still, since the All-Star break Elder has made three starts, going 2-0 with a 2.12 ERA, and in his most recent outing threw six strong innings against Washington. Miami's tNERD (9.61) is the story on the offensive side — young, cheap, and running well — but that's offset by a bullpen that's a wreck, with four key relievers all on the injured list, which could turn a tight pitchers' duel into a late-inning track meet. With a 14.27 gNERD, this sits comfortably above both the historic and today's averages, making it one of the more watchable matchups on the board.

Chicago White Sox @ Boston Red Sox, 4:10p

Summary

Boston is baseball's hottest team right now, and this White Sox-Red Sox matchup gives it a real pitching duel to go with the offense. The Red Sox have won 24 of their last 27 games, riding a five-game winning streak over Chicago into this one, including a 14-2 win Tuesday featuring a season-high four home runs, Caleb Durbin's first career grand slam, and a pair of homers from Wilyer Abreu. That's a tough act to follow, but the pitching matchup looks better than the box score suggests: Sean Burke owns the higher pNERD here, backed by strong strikeout stuff and a favorable xFIP-, while Sonny Gray brings similarly stingy xFIP- numbers despite diminished velocity and a plodding pace that dings his score. Tampa Bay Rays @ Colorado Rockies, 12:10p

Summary

This one's a skippable Wednesday matinee: two last-place-adjacent vibes colliding at altitude, with neither pitcher offering much swing-and-miss appeal. The Rays arrive as AL East front-runners enjoying a lead of 24 games over Colorado in the standings, so the playoff implications run in one direction only, while the Rockies are simply playing out the string in Denver. Nick Martinez has been a control artist rather than a strikeout machine — he enters with a 2.77 ERA across 21 outings, a 1.10 WHIP, and a strikeout rate of just 14 percent — and his modest pNERD (2.78) reflects that low-whiff, pound-the-zone approach. Sugano's surface numbers look better than his stuff deserves; his xFIP paints an uglier picture than his gaudy win total, and pitching at Coors is never a friendly proving ground for a soft-tossing sinker/splitter arm. Colorado's offense (tNERD 0.88, barely above the season floor) is thin, and the Rays' own barrel-rate woes keep their tNERD only middling. With a gNERD of 4.56 — well below the historic average of roughly 10 and near the bottom of today's slate — this is one to have on in the background at most.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Milwaukee Brewers, 4:40p

Summary

The Brewers own a massive division lead but the Pirates have quietly been their kryptonite lately, and this game pairs two of the more electric young arms in the league. Jared Jones just came back from a two-month injured-list stint and has rediscovered his stuff in July, posting a 2.00 ERA over five starts, and his velocity (98.5 mph average, a huge z-score outlier) and elite xFIP- back it up—hence a hearty 9.82 pNERD. Across from him, Logan Henderson has been arguably better on the ledger sheet, running a minuscule 70 xFIP- with a strong strikeout rate that lands him at 9.78 pNERD, continuing an 8-1 career run that includes a scoreless outing against the Giants his last time out. On the team side, Milwaukee's 9.17 tNERD is buoyed by a deep, young roster with strong baserunning and bullpen numbers, while Pittsburgh's 6.93 isn't far behind thanks to solid batting and baserunning of their own—fitting, given they've won four straight against the Brewers, including Monday's 4-3 series-opening upset. Add it up and you get a 17.85 gNERD, comfortably above both the historical and today's averages—this one's worth your evening.

Los Angeles Dodgers @ Chicago Cubs, 5:05p

Summary

Skubal traded to the Dodgers, making his debut against a lineup that isn't even his old team — that's the headline here, and it's a legitimately fun watch. This is Tarik Skubal's first start as a Dodger, coming to Wrigley just days after L.A. sent a package to Detroit to get him, and his 12.51 pNERD says the hype is earned. His shiny surface stats undersell it: Skubal carries a 31.0% strikeout rate with just a 3.7% walk rate this season, and his 0.910 WHIP ranks among the best in baseball, and his swinging-strike and strike-rate z-scores are near the top of the league, backed by a stingy xFIP-. He's also been on a run before the trade — in his past six outings, Skubal has given up only eight earned runs in 37 innings for an ERA of 1.95 — so this isn't just name value. Assad is a solid, unspectacular caretaker in the back half of the rotation with a low swinging-strike rate that drags his pNERD to a modest 2.75, and the Cubs are missing several top arms this series, which only widens the pitching gap. Both offenses carry real thump, though: the Dodgers' bat-heavy, deep lineup and a Cubs defense with an outstanding fielding number both push their tNERDs near 9.3, among the best pairings you'll see today or in the wider dataset, and Wrigley Field adds ambiance to a gNERD score (16.90) that ranks near the top of the pack.

This series opener slugfest sequel has real upside: the Yankees are chasing a bounce-back after Monday's wild 13-7 loss where Alec Burleson hit three homers off them, and Tuesday brings a legitimately compelling pitching matchup to boot. Ryan Weathers, the Yankees' lefty, owns the better peripherals here — his 79 xFIP- and 8.36 pNERD suggest he's pitching better than his 3.99 ERA lets on, and he's actually been a bit unlucky, so there's more in the tank than the raw numbers show. Hunter Dobbins, back from an ACL tear that ended his Red Sox tenure and now starting for St. Louis after the offseason trade for Willson Contreras, brings a solid 6.00 pNERD and a lively 95-plus mph fastball. New York's lineup is banged up — Aaron Judge (rib), Giancarlo Stanton (leg), and Cody Bellinger (leg) are all out — but the Yankees still post an 8.07 tNERD thanks to elite barrel rates and a deep bullpen, comfortably above both the historic and today's-game averages. Add in a Cardinals offense that just dropped 13 runs on this same pitching staff, and the 13.95 gNERD checks out: this one lands well above the historic median and near the top of today's slate.

Jesús Luzardo brings swing-and-miss stuff and a Nationals lineup that's mashing everything not named Luzardo, making this the rare Nats-Phillies game worth clearing your schedule for. Luzardo carries a strikeout rate near 29% and a tidy 3.57 ERA into the outing, though he's looking to bounce back from allowing six runs in 6.1 innings to the Marlins last time out, after allowing just eight earned runs in 49.1 innings across his previous eight starts. His pNERD of 10.58 backs that up — well above the 95th percentile for today's games — thanks to a strong xFIP-, plush velocity, and a bit of positive regression coming his way. Littell, by contrast, is scuffling for a Washington rotation gutted by injuries; the Nationals have DJ Herz, Josiah Gray, Mitchell Parker, Ken Waldichuk, and Connelly Early all on the injured list, leaving the club relying heavily on Littell despite his 5.94 FIP and negative WAR. That mismatch drags the pitching side down, but Washington's offense — young, athletic, and running wild on the bases — pushes the Nationals' tNERD to 9.24, comfortably above the historic 95th percentile. Philadelphia's bullpen depth and broadcast ratings add just enough polish to make the 13.19 gNERD a solidly above-average watch.

Cantillo, meanwhile, is the steadier arm of the two—his most recent start was four shutout innings against Cincinnati, a bounce-back from two rough outings that saw him give up 15 hits and nine runs over 8.2 innings—and his 5.43 pNERD edges Manaea's slightly on the back of a strong swinging-strike rate. Cleveland's tNERD (7.27) comfortably outpaces the Mets' (4.73), thanks to a young, cheap roster that grades out well on baserunning and payroll efficiency. The 11.30 gNERD lands almost exactly at today's average, so treat this as a solid midweek option rather than a can't-miss.

Minnesota Twins @ Kansas City Royals, 4:40p

Good stuff here — Dobnak's comeback story and Ryan's slump are exactly the color needed.

A former Twins washout is quietly outdueling his old team's ace, and that oddity alone makes this worth a glance — even if the underlying NERD math says skip it. Kansas City's Randy Dobnak, who was designated for assignment and bounced to the Mariners before Kansas City picked him up, has been the story of this series: Dobnak, the longtime Twin who was acquired by Kansas City from Seattle in June, has been outstanding since his debut with the Royals on July 2. Just last Wednesday he tossed seven shutout innings against his former club, permitting four hits and one walk in seven innings while striking out four, matching a career high and marking the first time he'd thrown more than 100 pitches in a start. Joe Ryan, meanwhile, is scuffling — he's 1-4 with a 4.91 ERA over his last six starts, allowing 12 runs and 18 hits in 10 innings of the past two — though his xFIP- of 87 still says he's the better bet on paper, and he owns this game's only pitcher NERD score of note (6.23) thanks to strong strike-throwing and whiff rates. Dobnak's pNERD (3.14) is a mirage built on a tidy ERA rather than real stuff. Team-wise, both clubs are duds: Minnesota's bullpen and defense are dragging its tNERD to 2.73, and Kansas City's bullpen (-36.5 runs) is arguably the worst in the league, propping up its 3.01 mark only via positive luck. Los Angeles Dodgers @ Chicago Cubs, 5:05p

Summary

This one has real juice: two 60-plus-win rivals, elite defenses, and a Cubs offense trying to snap out of a funk against a Dodgers club nursing a bruised ego after getting swept by Boston. The gNERD of 14.45 sits well above both the historical average (10.11) and today's slate (10.80), driven almost entirely by two outstanding team profiles — Dodgers (9.41) and Cubs (9.31) both rank near the top of the historic tNERD distribution, fueled by strong batting runs and, in the Cubs' case, an absurd fielding-runs mark of 55.6. The Dodgers arrive looking to reset after Dave Roberts admitted "They outplayed us" in a series where Boston outscored Los Angeles 20-10 over the three games, costing them the best record in baseball. Matthew Boyd (5.19 pNERD, solid strike-throwing and respectable xFIP-) takes the mound for Chicago, while the Dodgers' listed TBD starter is actually expected to be Justin Wrobleski, who enters with a 2.88 ERA over 112.2 IP despite peripherals suggesting he's been pretty lucky this year. Add in a Cubs bullpen that's shaky and a Dodgers pen anchored by a bounced-back Tanner Scott, and this is a legitimately watchable ballgame.

St. Louis Cardinals @ New York Yankees, 4:05p

Summary

Cam Schlittler's electric arm makes this one worth catching, even if the Cardinals side of the ledger looks bleak. This is Schlittler's Cy Young-caliber season on display — the right-hander carries a 2.04 ERA and has struck out 165 batters this season, backed by a blistering four-seam fastball that sits at 97.9 mph and generates a 30.4% whiff rate with a .234 xwOBA against. His pNERD of 10.54 is comfortably above today's average and sits near the top of the historical distribution, fueled by elite strikeout stuff and top-shelf velocity. McGreevy, by contrast, is scuffling badly — his last outing saw him come against the Cubs on July 28, one of the roughest starts of his season, lasting only 1⅔ innings while allowing seven earned runs — and his 3.67 pNERD reflects thin whiff and strike-rate numbers. The Yankees' 8.16 tNERD, boosted by strong barrel rate and baserunning marks, dwarfs a punchless Cardinals lineup dealing with a slump; St. Louis has fallen under .500 with seven losses in their last 10 games and sits four games out of the final wild card spot. New York is banged up too, with Aaron Judge, Cody Bellinger, and Carlos Rodón all on the injured list, but that hardly dents this gNERD of 13.82, which lands well above both the historical and today's averages — mostly on the strength of one dominant arm.

With gNERD at 13.12, well above the historical average and near today's top mark, this is one of the day's better bets.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Boston Red Sox @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 6:10p

Summary

I have enough information from my searches to write a well-supported summary.

Payton Tolle's first look at a Dodgers lineup loaded with October ghosts is the story here, and the Dodgers' star-studded roster combined with a legitimate pitching duel makes this one of the day's better watches. Tolle, Boston's former second-round pick and top pitching prospect, made his major-league debut just last summer against Paul Skenes and the Pirates, and this outing gives fans a chance to see the 23-year-old lefty—armed with elite extension and a five-pitch mix—test himself against a genuine championship-caliber lineup rather than a rebuilding club.A rookie fireballer taking on a stacked Dodgers lineup, in a game that ranks near the top of the day's watchability charts—this one's worth clearing your schedule for. The gNERD of 16.18 sits comfortably above both today's average (11.35) and the historic norm (10.11), driven largely by the Dodgers' tNERD of 9.48, one of the stronger offensive-and-defensive packages you'll see, powered by elite batting runs and a barrel rate that would make any pitcher nervous. Boston's 5.86 tNERD is more middling, propped up by a strong bullpen and a bit of positive luck suggesting they've actually underperformed their true talent level.

On the mound, Payton Tolle, the Red Sox's second-round pick out of TCU, was ranked as the team's No. 2 prospect, compiling a 3.44 ERA with 133 strikeouts in 91 2/3 innings before rocketing to the majors. His pNERD of 9.06 reflects excellent strike-throwing and swinging-strike marks for a 23-year-old with mid-90s velocity. Yamamoto counters with a 7.95 pNERD, anchored by a sparkling 79 xFIP-, making this a legitimately compelling pitching matchup wrapped around a lopsided but entertaining lineup mismatch.

Matt Olson (29 homers) and James Wood (30, fifth in the NL) headline lineups that should keep the ball flying, and that fits the Nationals' hefty 9.69 tNERD — buoyed by strong barrel rates, baserunning, and a young, cheap roster — against Atlanta's more middling 6.15. Washington sits 10.5 games back with the division race essentially over, but the roster still has juice even if the bullpen (a serious liability, worth -2.06 in components) keeps blowing it.

On the mound, neither arm brings much shine: Mikolas is struggling at a 5.65 ERA with just three wins for Washington and his tiny 0.1% SwStr rate signals real swing-and-miss issues, though positive luck suggests some correction could be coming. López is steadier — carrying a 3.64 ERA and four wins, a reliable mid-rotation arm — but neither profile screams "must-watch." Add in Luis García Jr.'s day-to-day knee issue and a thinned-out Nationals pitching staff, and this lands as a solidly average game — decent lineups, unremarkable arms, watch for the homers rather than the pitching.

entry.content:

  • Generated by the mlb-watchability project on GitHub.

Detail

Pittsburgh Pirates @ Cincinnati Reds, 3:10p

Summary

Two of the best arms in baseball facing off means this one's a must-watch, even if the box scores haven't been kind to one of them. This game's 17.34 gNERD sits near the top of both today's slate (average 11.09) and the historical distribution (95th percentile is 14.76), and the pitching matchup is the reason why. Paul Skenes brings his usual excellence — a 2.72 FIP, 30.4% strikeout rate, and only a 5.7% walk rate this season — and has been particularly nasty against Cincinnati, owning a 5-0 record with a 1.38 ERA, 52 strikeouts and six walks over 39 innings in his career against the Reds. Hunter Greene's actual pNERD-topping 12.25 tells a different story than his ugly 7.06 ERA suggests: his underlying peripherals (3.20 FIP, 3.09 xFIP) suggest his results have been far worse than his stuff, a classic case of bad luck (and a return from an early-season elbow injury) masking real swing-and-miss ability. The Reds' offense has been genuinely poor this year, dragging their tNERD down, while the Pirates counter with solid baserunning and pop but shaky defense. Elly De La Cruz has been a standout at home, hitting .320 with a .970 OPS and 10 home runs in 172 at-bats at Great American Ball Park, giving Skenes at least one dangerous bat to navigate.

New York Yankees @ Chicago Cubs, 11:20a

Summary

Good stuff — plenty of storylines here. Let me write the summary.

A Wrigley Field matinee with real fielding wizardry and an offense-vs-lefty-with-a-barrel-problem subplot makes this the most watchable game on the board today. Both tNERD marks are near the top of what we've seen this year — the Cubs' 9.23 is boosted by elite team defense (fielding runs cratering z-scores at 3.10) and a strong batting attack, while the Yankees check in at 8.54 thanks to raw power (top-tier barrel rate) and baserunning value, even while missing Aaron Judge, who landed on the 60-day injured list with a rib injury and, as of the latest team updates, was still working through scans before resuming baseball activities, plus Cody Bellinger and Giancarlo Stanton. Imanaga is the headliner on the mound, a lefty who has a 1.10 WHIP that dwarfs Will Warren's 1.41, and who's coming off an outstanding July, posting a 1.19 ERA across four starts, including back-to-back scoreless outings. Warren, by contrast, has been rough lately — allowing six earned runs in three innings in his last outing, part of a subpar July where he's 0-2 with a 7.50 ERA — though his xFIP still checks out fine underneath the noise. Pete Crow-Armstrong versus a shorthanded Yankees lineup is worth watching too.

Detail

New York Yankees @ Chicago White Sox, 11:10a

Summary

A first-place showdown with a red-hot White Sox ace and a fading Yankees lineup down to its studs — this one has drama even if the box score might not be pretty for New York. Chicago sits atop the AL Central and gets a huge boost from Sean Burke, who has been red hot as of late, posting a 1.61 ERA since his last start against New York in mid-June, backing up his solid 6.66 pNERD with a tidy xFIP- of 89. Ryan Weathers actually rates a touch higher on pure stuff (8.84 pNERD, xFIP- of 77), but Weathers's last five starts have produced an ERA of 5.5, and he's without some serious offensive help — Aaron Judge is out, Giancarlo Stanton is out, Cody Bellinger is out. Both clubs carry matching 8.48-8.49 tNERD scores, with the White Sox's youthful, discount-payroll roster and the Yankees' power/baserunning combo each pulling real weight. With a 16.24 gNERD, this game ranks well above both the historical median and today's slate average, making it one of the stronger watches on the board. Add a tight division race and a lopsided season head-to-head — Yankees are 4-2 against Chicago this year — and there's plenty of subplot even before the first pitch.

Miami Marlins @ New York Mets, 4:10p

Summary

A rookie phenom with elite stuff against a hard-throwing 23-year-old Marlins arm, wrapped around a Miami team that just snapped a 12-game losing streak in dramatic fashion — this one's worth your evening. Nolan McLean has been arguably the Mets' best story of the season, carrying a 79 xFIP- and a 2.17 ERA in 58.0 innings over his last 10 starts dating back to May 31, and his 8.61 pNERD reflects a genuinely dominant, young power arm. Eury Pérez counters with 98-mph heat and a well above-average swinging-strike rate, giving this game two of the more compelling starters you'll see on a given day. Miami arrives with real juice: after setting a franchise record with 12 consecutive losses, Miami has rattled off three straight wins to stabilize, including a dominant stretch against Philadelphia that featured Sandy Alcantara's return to form and late-game heroics from Griffin Conine. The Marlins' 9.84 tNERD is buoyed by strong baserunning and a favorable luck score suggesting more contention ahead, while the Mets, missing Juan Soto and Mark Vientos to injury, limp in with a middling offense. Combined, the 15.39 gNERD sits well above both the historical average and today's slate, making this one of the sharper watches on the board.

Seattle Mariners @ Los Angeles Dodgers, 7:10p

Summary

I'll proceed with the information gathered so far, since I have solid material on Sasaki and the Dodgers/Mariners context.

A juicy pitching duel with two of the game's most electric arms, even if one of them is still finding his footing. Roki Sasaki brings triple-digit stuff and a season of turbulence to Dodger Stadium, while Bryan Woo quietly continues to be one of the more efficient strike-throwers in the league — this is a game where the gNERD score of 14.40 sits well above both the historical average (10.11) and even today's slate average (11.63), and it shows.

Sasaki's command has been shaky since returning to the rotation, with 69 hits and 38 walks in 70 innings and his ERA climbing to 5.88 in seven starts this year. He's even dealt with a start against San Diego where the opposition seemed to be sitting on everything he threw, though his velocity remains elite — his 97.8 mph average sits well above league norms and drives most of his 8.25 pNERD. Woo, by contrast, is a model of efficiency: his strike-throwing and command (73rd-percentile strike rate, low walk totals) push his pNERD to 7.93 despite modest raw stuff, and he's currently running well ahead of his peripherals on the luck front, suggesting some regression toward even better results isn't out of the question. On the team side, the Dodgers' 9.52 tNERD is elite, built on top-tier batting runs and barrel rate, while Seattle's 3.11 is closer to replacement level — so expect fireworks from the lineup wearing blue.

Jake Irvin's return from a two-month shoulder absence is the real hook here, and it comes with a twist of dramatic irony: he tore up his shoulder in this very matchup back in May, mid-way through a hitless outing against Atlanta.
